2611.33326.abstract: Spatially resolved galaxy properties are routinely derived from integral-field spectroscopy and increasingly from multi-band photometry as a wealth of photometric data become available in large surveys like LSST/Rubin. Spatially resolved star formation histories (SFHs) offer a detailed view of galaxy growth and quenching by tracing the timing and location of star formation within a galaxy up to one billion years in the past. However, stellar migration between spaxels may strongly bias these reconstructions. Quantifying this bias remains challenging as few Milky-Way mass simulations fully resolve initial stellar dispersions or migration rates. We use the well-validated h277 Milky-Way-mass cosmological zoom simulation, which resolves both via explicitly tying star formation to the non-equilibrium abundance of H2, to assess the quality of specific star formation rates (sSFR) radial profiles inferred from resolved SFHs against actual values from stellar particle tracking. Across several evolutionary windows spanning a range of stellar activity stages from quiescent to star-bursting, we find that the adaptive radial binning imposed by S/N constraints in photometric SED fitting actually mitigates most of the blurring/mixing effects of stellar migration on inferred radial profiles up to lookback times of 1.5 Gyr. This allows for proper recovery of not only the average sSFR but also its radial slope, its relative changes in scatter across radial annuli and even approximate localization of low-z star-forming clumps. Only galaxies having undergone a major merger across the considered lookback time display discrepant, unreliable sSFR profiles, hence should not be considered for such reconstructions.

2611.33435.abstract: Variability in active galactic nuclei (AGNs) is remarkably diverse, spanning multiple timescales, wavelengths, and physical processes. Variability probes accretion physics and the interplay between supermassive black holes and their surroundings. Building on early case studies, the field has shifted toward population-level analyses of increasingly large datasets, making scalable techniques crucial for upcoming time-domain surveys. We developed a Python-based pipeline to analyze AGN light curves using variability metrics and applied it to 14,061 nearby AGNs ($z\lesssim 0.09$) observed with ZTF. We examined metric distributions and correlations. Amplitude-based metrics (e.g., $F_{\rm var}$) help identify major flares but are sensitive to single deviant epochs. Temporal metrics such as $\eta$ provide a complementary check. Comparison with WISE infrared photometry suggests that $\eta$ traces the strength of AGN activity. Most Type~I and Type~II AGNs in our sample exhibit similar variability patterns based on these metrics. This overlap may partly reflect misclassifications that targeted spectroscopic follow-up could help resolve. To identify subsets of AGNs with distinctive variability, we used UMAP to group sources with similar metric values. The resulting embedding shows a region enriched in high-amplitude variables, including a subset with long-term flux trends. We find evidence that extremely variable quasars and changing-look AGNs may populate this region, which can help prioritize sources for follow-up. Our pipeline offers a scalable, survey-agnostic framework suitable for application to Vera C. Rubin Observatory's LSST and other ongoing and upcoming photometric surveys.

2611.33624.abstract: The distribution of stellar mass between massive galaxies and their companions traces how galaxy assembly proceeds within early large-scale structure. We investigate the environments of two galaxies from the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) CRISTAL survey: CRISTAL-19 (C19; $z=5.235$) and CRISTAL-21 (C21; $z=5.256$), using F444W slitless spectroscopy from the Near-Infrared Camera (NIRCam) on the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) in COSMOS-3D. A friends-of-friends analysis of H$\alpha$ emitters identifies two distinct overdense nodes separated by approximately 25 comoving Mpc. Although C21 is the more massive galaxy, C19 has the more massive, actively star-forming companions. The companion populations around C19 and C21 have median stellar masses of $\log(M_\star/M_\odot)=9.43$ and 8.82 and median dust-corrected H$\alpha$ star formation rates of 31 and $16~M_\odot~\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, respectively. Their star formation rate contrast largely reflects the difference in companion masses. C19 contains only $4.5^{+0.9}_{-0.7}\%$ of the combined measured stellar mass of itself and its selected companions; the corresponding fraction for C21 is $39^{+5}_{-5}\%$. Thus, stellar mass remains more widely distributed among galaxies around C19, whereas a larger share resides in C21. Resolved interacting companions around C19 and [C II] kinematics consistent with a late-stage merger in C21 support this contrast in assembly state. These findings support the phase-dependent picture of Zou et al. (2026), in which the surrounding star-forming population changes as interactions and mergers build up a massive galaxy.

2611.33660.abstract: We investigate a method for inferring the local dark matter (DM) density in the solar neighbourhood using a deep learning framework that learns the mapping between stellar kinematics and the underlying DM density field from cosmological simulations. To this end, we construct a training set from 7 Milky Way-like galaxies in the FIRE-2 simulation suite. We use three-dimensional stellar kinematic components, consisting of the tangential velocities along the right ascension and declination directions ($v_{\alpha*}$ and $v_{\delta}$) derived from parallaxes and proper motions, together with radial velocity, as input features to predict the three-dimensional DM density field. Two distinct architectures, VNet (arXiv:1606.04797) and ViT-VNet (arXiv:2205.08534), are trained on identical datasets. Both models reproduce the large-scale DM density gradient, whereas small-scale fluctuations are systematically smoothed. Applying the trained models to Gaia DR3 data yields our best estimates of the local DM density: $0.80^{+0.10}_{-0.10}$ and $1.12^{+0.15}_{-0.13}$ GeV cm$^{-3}$ from VNet and ViT-VNet, respectively. The quoted uncertainties reflect the inference scatter across the training set. We further examine systematics from model dependence and the simulation-Gaia domain mismatch, providing an initial step towards a framework for reconstructing local DM maps from future multi-epoch astrometric measurements, including those expected from Gaia DR4.

2611.33768.abstract: Through a retrospective search for tidal disruption events (TDEs) in the ZTF archives agnostic to their location within their host galaxies, we identify AT2024dky/ZTF24aagksvd as a promising off-nuclear TDE candidate. At $z=0.0592$, it lies at a projected offset of $3.72^{\prime\prime}$ (4.26 kpc) from the center of a massive ($M_{\rm gal}\sim10^{11}\,M_\odot$), quiescent galaxy. We present early-time ZTF and ATLAS optical photometry and late-time follow-up observations with Keck-I/LRIS, VLA, EP, and Chandra. With $M_{g,\rm peak}=-18.50$ mag, AT2024dky exhibits persistently blue color ($g-r\sim-0.1$ mag) through 80 d after peak. At $\delta t=858$ d, Keck reveals $M_{u'}=-13.07\pm0.09$ mag and $M_R > -14.15$ mag. At $\delta t=866$ d, VLA detects the transient at $u L_{u,10\,\rm GHz}=(1.26\pm0.17)\times10^{38}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$. The combination of early photometric evolution, detected late-time radio and UV emission strongly favor a TDE interpretation. The properties of its host galaxy also bear remarkable similarities to the parent galaxies of known off-nuclear TDEs. Based on the low values of peak-time and late-time UV/optical luminosities, we favor a black hole mass of $\sim 10^5$--$10^6 M_\odot$. Together, these observations strongly favor an off-nuclear TDE.

2611.33798.abstract: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has revealed a population of compact sources known as ``little red dots'' (LRDs), characterized by a distinctive V-shaped spectral energy distribution (SED) from UV to optical wavelengths. The physical nature of these sources remains debated. The ``black hole star'' (BH*) scenario, wherein a super-Eddington accreting black hole is embedded in a dense gaseous envelope, has been proposed to explain them. We assemble a sample of 22 LRDs at $4.0 \lesssim z \lesssim 9.5$ from the ASTRODEEP-JWST database. We construct a composite ``host galaxy + BH*'' model using the \texttt{Cloudy} photoionization code, and perform SED fitting with \textsc{BayeSED3}. Our modeling reproduces the observed V-shaped features: the UV continuum blueward of the Balmer break is well reproduced by stellar emission within this decomposition, while the optical regime is dominated by the BH* component. Our fits reveal that LRDs are black holes hosted by faint, low-mass galaxies with median stellar and black hole masses of $M_* = 10^{8.7}\,M_\odot$ and $M_{\rm BH} = 10^{6.4}\,M_\odot$, respectively. These black holes are moderately overmassive relative to local scaling relations but less extreme than broad-line estimates. The median bolometric luminosity $L_{\rm BH^*} \sim 10^{44.9}\,\rm erg\,s^{-1}$ mitigates the reported number density tension from 1--2 orders of magnitude to a factor of a few. The host galaxies lie near the high-redshift star-forming main sequence, and stellar extinction correlates positively with star formation rate (SFR). The BH* scenario provides a self-consistent paradigm for LRDs, offering insights into the rapid growth of supermassive black hole seeds and their co-evolution with host galaxies during the cosmic dawn.

2611.33899.abstract: Polarization directions provide a sensitive probe of Faraday rotation without weighting the signal by polarized brightness. We develop their spatial statistics for a turbulent volume in which synchrotron emission and Faraday rotation coexist. For independent, zero-mean Gaussian polarized emissivity, we derive an exact relation for the directional correlation. We derive strong stochastic coherence-depth scalings, including an additional interval for steep Faraday-density spectra, and distinguish them from the conditions needed to infer directional spectral slopes. We also quantify the weak-rotation response of a coherent uniform emitter and demonstrate that the scalings of the normalized tangential polarization gradient follow directly from the direction spectrum. A combined use of the techniques, including those introduced earlier in Lazarian & Pogosyan (2016), provides a way for detailed study of astrophysical turbulence.

2611.33956.abstract: To probe the role of hierarchical gas structures in massive star formation, we statistically analyzed 13 Galactic massive star-forming regions using FUGIN CO survey data. Applying a non-binary dendrogram to the position-position-velocity data, we classified the extracted structures into trunks, internal leaves (the densest substructures within trunks), and isolated structures, and compared their properties with an analysis of variance controlling for regional differences. In representative regions, the trunks correspond to morphologies such as filaments and hub-filament systems, or to kinematic signatures of structure-forming events such as cloud-cloud collisions. Across the sample, the trunks are extended, massive, and strongly bound reservoirs, while the leaves are significantly more massive, denser, and more tightly bound than isolated structures of similar spatial scale. Using YSOs and Hi-GAL clumps, we find that the leaves have a lower low-mass star formation efficiency than isolated structures, whereas their clump formation efficiency is comparable. At a fixed gas mass, the leaves show no higher low-mass star formation efficiency than isolated structures but convert a larger fraction of their gas into dense clumps. We interpret these contrasts, together with inward gas motions in the position-velocity diagrams, as indicating that the deep potential of the trunks sustains continuous accretion onto the leaves and promotes mutual interactions among them. These processes may raise the characteristic fragmentation mass, as theoretically expected for a dynamically accreting medium, so that a larger fraction of the gas forms massive clumps without a corresponding increase in low-mass star formation. Our single-epoch data constrain only these structural contrasts, but indicate that the gas available for massive star formation is organized on scales larger than a single core.

2611.34144.abstract: High-redshift Little Red Dots (LRDs) are radio faint in existing survey and deep-field samples. Nearby LRD analogues allow the radio emission and spectra of individual sources to be measured, which is not possible at $z\sim6$. Our sample comprises 44 low-redshift LRDs ($0.101 \leq z \leq 0.882$) . Eight objects are radio-detected: five at 144\,MHz with LoTSS, six at 3\,GHz with VLASS at $\geq3\sigma$, and J1047 through its published VLA data. The rest-frame 144\,MHz luminosities of the LoTSS detections span $1.8\times10^{30}$ to $3.6\times10^{31}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}\,Hz^{-1}}$. The LoTSS--VLASS spectral indices range from $-0.27\pm0.04$ (J2048) to $-0.78\pm0.11$ (J1200). J1051 lacks 144\,MHz coverage and has $\alpha_{0.9 \rm GHz}^{\rm 3 GHz} \simeq-0.93$. J1047 has a clear deficit at 144 MHz relative to its optically thin GHz spectrum, consistent with a turnover whose position and physical mechanism are not uniquely constrained by the archival data. The higher detection fraction among the Green Pea sample largely reflects their lower redshift: in this subsample LoTSS reaches luminosities roughly an order of magnitude fainter than in the more distant DESI gold sample. If their escaping spectra and radio luminosities are held fixed and extrapolated as power laws, the five LoTSS detections would have observed-frame 144 MHz flux densities of $\sim0.7$--$32\,\mu\mathrm{Jy}$. Low-redshift LRDs span more than an order of magnitude in radio luminosity among the detections, and more than two orders of magnitude when the J1047 upper limit is included. They also show several distinct spectral shapes, so the optically defined LRD class encompasses diverse radio properties. Current detection statistics are strongly shaped by redshift and survey sensitivity. The source-by-source luminosity limits provide a reference for interpreting future LRD samples.

2611.34149.abstract: The aim of this paper is to use the Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU) to assess the fraction of high-z quasi-stellar objects (QSOs) that are radio-emitting at ~0.2 mJy/beam level and to establish if the radio emission is mainly produced by relativistic jets. A sample of 808 type1 QSOs in the redshift range 4<z<9 and covering the sky area currently observed by EMU was compiled from the literature and the SDSS spectroscopic database and cross-matched with EMU source catalogue. In total, 124 high-z QSOs are detected by EMU, corresponding to 15% of the sample. The large majority (70%) of the QSOs radio detected by EMU are reported in the radio for the first time. We use this sample to establish the detection rate at different optical magnitudes. We show that the fraction of radio-loud (R>10) high-z QSOs is about 8% while the fraction of radio detections is a strong function of the optical magnitude and reaches values of ~35% when only the optically brightest (mag~18) QSOs are considered. Since all the radio detected QSOs, including those classified as radio-quiet (R<10), exhibit radio powers ranging from 5x10^24 to 5x10^27 W Hz^-1 at 5 GHz, we argue that they could all host a relativistic jet and that orientation could be one of the main causes of the different values of radio-loudness observed in the sample. To support this hypothesis, we show that the number of high-z QSOs detected by EMU is fully consistent with the predictions based on the beaming model, using as reference the high-z blazars discovered at higher radio flux densities. The results presented here suggest that relativistic jets could have been very common in the early Universe representing up to ~35% of the luminous (L_1450A>10^46 erg s^-1) QSO population. Future observations with SKAO will be instrumental to unambiguously confirm the jetted nature of the QSOs currently detected by EMU.

2611.34198.abstract: Bars are common structures in disk galaxies that can strongly influence the evolution of their hosts. Simulations predict that bars formed through tidal interactions tend to rotate slower than bars formed in isolation. We test this prediction observationally by studying the kinematics of 314 bars in galaxies between $0.016<z<0.130$. We use estimates of the bar pattern speed ($\Omega_p$) and the rotation rate ($\mathcal{R}$) obtained from four studies using IFU data from the MaNGA survey. We cross-match the host galaxies of the bars to the Galaxy Zoo DESI catalogue in order to study their environment and classify each galaxy as paired or isolated. We find that bars that are slower in terms of $\mathcal{R}$ are more likely to be found in paired galaxies. The fraction of bars in paired galaxies increases from $5^{+6}_{-2}\%$ for $0<\mathcal{R}<1.0$ to $31^{+15}_{-9}\%$ for $3.0<\mathcal{R}<4.0$. Our results also suggest a possible difference in the distribution of $\mathcal{R}$ between paired (mean $\mathcal{R}=2.1 \pm 0.2$) and isolated (mean $\mathcal{R}=1.75 \pm 0.07$) galaxies (p-value=0.037; 2.09$\sigma$). On the other hand, our analysis reveals no noticeable trend between the fraction of paired galaxies and the bar pattern speed, which indicates that the pattern speed is not correlated with the likelihood of a galaxy being paired. We also find no difference in the distribution of $\Omega_p$ between paired and isolated galaxies (p-value$>$0.250; $<$1.15$\sigma$).

2611.34625.abstract: The Milky Way's disc is warped in a way that varies depending on the age of the population considered. We, for the first time, trace that kinematics of the warp in red clumps stars. This means that our sample is drawn from a consistent population across the disc, composed of standard candles that allow for precise distance estimates but, unlike samples of Cepheid variables, is relatively old. We find that, consistent with other populations, the red-clump warp is precessing at ${\sim}12\;{\rm km}\,{\rm s}^{-1}\,{\rm kpc}^{-1}$, comparable to the angular velocity of stars around the Galaxy in the outer reaches of the disc. Unlike younger populations, the kinematic signature is offset from that which we would expect given the stellar positions. This reinforces the conclusion that the Milky Way's warp is dynamically evolving, making this a necessary property of any model that seeks to explain its creation.

2611.34691.abstract: We report the first interstellar detection of the higher-energy $s$-cis conformer of acrolein (CH2CHCHO) toward TMC-1 using the Quijote line survey. Local thermodynamic equilibrium modeling, assuming a rotational temperature of 7.5 K, yields a column density of $(1.0\pm0.2)\times10^{11}$~cm$^{-2}$ when fitting the observed lines. The s-cis/s-trans abundance ratio is $0.45\pm0.11$, despite an energy separation of approximately 1025~K, indicating a strongly nonequilibrium conformational distribution. An exploratory gas--grain chemical model identifies C3H5 + O as the dominant acrolein formation route, pointing to this reaction as a first entry to consider when explaining the isomeric ratios. The observed ratio provides a new constraint on conformer-specific formation, destruction, and interconversion processes in cold interstellar clouds.

2611.34743.abstract: Galaxy-formation models rely on accreting black holes to expel gas from their hosts. We test this prediction in 67 little red dots (LRDs) and little blue dots (LBDs) in the first 1.5 billion years, selected from 80,367 NIRSpec spectra in the DAWN JWST Archive. We detect no [O III] wind, against lower limits of 7.2 and 7.5 expected detections for local sub-Eddington and super-Eddington active nuclei. For winds narrower than 1,500 km/s, the corresponding incidence limits are 13% and 19% at 95% confidence, compared with 31% and 49% locally. Broad Balmer lines are centred on the narrow lines, and Balmer absorbers move below 8% of the escape speed. Published super-Eddington fountain, black-hole-star and quasi-star models each fail a measured property of the spectra. LRDs and LBDs drive no superwinds, and their black holes grow without the wind feedback invoked to regulate galaxies.

2611.34775.abstract: We present four newly discovered Milky Way satellites from a systematic search through the $gri$ photometry from the Ultraviolet Near-Infrared Optical Northern Survey (UNIONS). Two of these satellites are likely ultra-faint dwarf galaxies that we have named Boötes VI and Draco III. Both galaxy candidates are $\gtrsim 100$ kpc from the Galactic center and have absolute $V$-band magnitudes ($M_V$) of $-2.7^{+0.6}_{-0.5}$ and $-4.0\pm0.6$, respectively. Boötes VI and Draco III have physical half-light radii ($r_{\rm h}$) of $\sim 50$ pc, or about twice as large as the most extended Milky Way globular clusters with similar luminosities. They are therefore candidate galaxies, though chemodynamical analyses will be needed to secure these classifications. We name the two other systems UNIONS 2 and UNIONS 3. They are extremely faint ($M_V = +0.4^{+0.6}_{-0.9}$ and $-0.7^{+0.6}_{-0.8}$) and compact ($r_{\rm h} = 5\,\pm\,1$ and $10^{+3}_{-2} pc), and zero giant stars are identified in either of their present-day stellar populations. Morphological measurements alone are not sufficient to assess the presence of dark matter in either system, so do not provide definitive classifications. We discuss the challenges in either detecting or refuting the presence of dark matter in UNIONS 2 and UNIONS 3, two systems that are archetypal of the faintest satellites that will be discovered in increasing numbers in upcoming wide-field surveys.

2611.34802.abstract: The spectral energy distribution (SED) of a galaxy encodes vital information about its chemical composition, stellar populations, and dust content. To model the infrared emission, many modern SED-fitting codes rely on dust energy balance, which assumes that all energy absorbed by dust in the UV-optical is equal to the energy emitted by dust in the infrared regime. However, few studies have been carried out to test the validity of this assumption at high redshift, where direct infrared observations are sparse. In this work, we perform aperture photometry in 111 galaxies from the Blue Jay survey ($1.7 < z < 3.5$) using public JWST/MIRI observations from the PRIMER, COSMOS-Web and COSMOS-3D surveys. Focusing on a subsample of 89 star-forming galaxies, we reconstruct best-fit SED model spectra from Prospector using only HST and NIRCam photometry and compare the predicted mid-infrared fluxes to the measured MIRI photometry. We find that mid-infrared fluxes are systematically overpredicted by about 10% at 7.7$\mu$m up to a factor of $\sim3$ at 21$\mu$m. The discrepancy increases with inferred dust attenuation, indicating that dust energy balance suffers from line-of-sight effects in systems with complex dust geometries. We find that adding NIRSpec spectroscopy to the fits breaks parameter degeneracies and strongly reduces the overprediction. When fitting the measured MIRI photometry together with the HST and NIRCam data, the best-fit model spectra of dusty galaxies ($A_V\gtrsim1$) result in significantly lower infrared luminosities by -0.6 dex compared to best-fit spectra obtained without MIRI, consistent with steeper, SMC-like attenuation curves or complex star-dust geometries. Our study highlights the limitations of dust energy balance at high redshift and underlines the importance of direct observations for accurately recovering the ISM and dust properties of galaxies at cosmic noon.

2611.34890.abstract: We investigate the chemo-dynamical properties of in-situ stars in the Galactic bar region (central $5$ kpc), specifically the inner Galactic counterpart of the solar-neighbourhood Splash population (in situ halo). We use a sample of APOGEE DR17 red giants with Gaia astrometry and AstroNN distances, and separate bulge/bar stellar populations dynamically using a normalised time-averaged bar-frame angular momentum, $\mathcal{V}_{\phi}$. Chemo-dynamical maps in the $\mathcal{V}_{\phi}$-[Fe/H] plane reveal a pronounced extension of the bar population towards $\mathcal{V}_{\phi}<0$ (non-bar-following orbits) within $-1.0<{\rm [Fe/H]}<-0.3$, characterised by high eccentricities, large $z_{\rm max}$ and an extended spheroidal orbit density distribution, and accounting for $\sim 30\%$ of all stars at these metallicities. These $\mathcal{V}_{\phi}<0$ stars have [Mg/Fe] and [Al/Fe] abundances similar to those of stars on ${\rm x_1}$ orbits at the same [Fe/H], and they match the solar-neighbourhood Splash in its metallicity and abundance ratio distributions. We therefore refer to them as the $\textit{central Splash}$. The presence of a significant central Splash underscores the role of the Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus merger in the early history of the Galaxy. We find a similar, weaker extension in the $\mathcal{V}_{\phi}$-[Fe/H] maps for extremely metal-rich stars, which are confined to the bulge. At metallicities [Fe/H] $<0.3$, we find no additional classical bulge population in these maps beyond the central Splash and proto-Galactic populations $-$ the high-$\alpha$ bulge appears to have evolved from the early high-$\alpha$ disc.

2611.34910.abstract: We model 3 and 10 $\mu$m dust grains in supersonic, turbulent molecular cloud conditions to compare two different numerical methods solving dust coupled to gas through a drag term. One method models dust and gas as two separate species (two fluid) and the other the combination of dust and gas as a single mixture (one fluid) using the diffusion approximation. Simulations are performed in a 3D periodic box using the Phantom code. The gas probability distributions are consistent with a lognormal distribution for both methods and grain sizes. The dust distributions are different in the two methods, showing discrepancies particularly in regions of low density. The most significant difference between the two methods is in the dust-to-gas ratio distributions. Both methods peak at the mean dust-to-gas ratio of 0.01, but the two-fluid method has wider distributions than the one-fluid method suggesting excess dust concentration in dense filaments. Filaments are where the one-fluid method results are most accurate. The narrowing of the one-fluid distribution is also caused by the stopping time limiter used to maintain the terminal velocity approximation. This artificially makes the mixture more coupled in low-density regions. Our overall conclusion is that both methods are viable for the study of dust in molecular clouds, but that the correct method should be chosen based on the numerical Stokes number regime of the calculation to avoid numerical artifacts.

2611.31340.abstract: Radiation transport is an essential process in many physical simulations, including cosmological codes which track stellar and diffuse radiation. Many present codes utilize ray tracing or moment methods, but these grow increasingly difficult and expensive for large simulations. Quantum lattice Boltzmann methods exponentially reduce complexity by propagating radiation over a lattice, allowing for better spatial resolution without needing to introduce adaptive ray tracing or other optimizations. However, existing formulations result in poor angular resolution for radiation point sources. In this work, we propose an angular redistribution methodology which significantly improves the resolution with minimal increase in complexity. We verify the correctness of the method on both classical processors and quantum simulators and outline how the quantum algorithm can be integrated into existing codes. This method is an important step towards fully-quantum radiation hydrodynamics simulation which could exponentially accelerate existing cosmological codes, enabling simulations at scales currently infeasible.

2611.33282.abstract: As scientific datasets grow in complexity and precision, the primary source of uncertainty in parameter inference shifts from measurement noise to systematic errors within the simulators themselves. In this setting, Bayesian evidence concentrates on whichever misspecified model best approximates the data. Evidence-weighted model averaging can then underestimate systematic uncertainty when one model component compensates for the misspecification of another component. We posit that in this case, the key question is how each model responds to discrepancies between simulator and data. We show that the local response of an inferred parameter to perturbations in the data --- the model's influence map --- can be estimated efficiently from forward evaluations of the simulator at existing posterior samples. Propagating discrepancy residuals through these influence maps enables individual sources of systematic bias to be isolated. Applied to independent observations used to infer the mass of a supermassive black hole, we find that the error is dominated by model systematics. We identify a simplification shared by all models, propagate the discrepancies through each model's influence map, and apply a first-order correction of the resulting biases. This substantially improves the cross-observation consistency of the inferred black-hole mass within each model while preserving the between-model spread that represents remaining systematics.

2611.33363.abstract: Ongoing and forthcoming wide-field surveys will discover $O(10^5)$ galaxy-galaxy strong lenses, shifting the main bottleneck from detection to reliable physical modeling. Conventional forward-modeling pipelines still rely on case-by-case expert judgment and manual tuning to mask contaminants, initialize priors, diagnose unphysical fits, and reconfigure failed runs. We present Lens-Orchestra, an automated workflow coupling a team of multimodal large language model agents to multi-stage physical modeling with elliptical power-law mass profiles, external shear, and pixelized source reconstructions. Launched via natural-language instructions, it modeled 185 Euclid Quick Data Release (Q1) grade-A lens candidates with published mass models without human intervention, completing 149 fits. Independent human evaluation confirmed 140 usable models, including 126 grade-I fits with noise-level residuals (with only 6.0% of completed fits unacceptable), and endorsed all 36 halted runs. Across the 140 usable systems, effective Einstein radii match released Q1 models (+0.12% median offset; 2.73% typical scatter), while hierarchical inference on the 126 grade-I imaging-only fits yields a mean mass-density slope of $2.002 \pm 0.009$ (intrinsic scatter $0.074^{+0.007}_{-0.006}$). A dedicated residual-screening agent also guided the selection of two candidate low-mass perturbers for parametric and free-form substructure modeling; although neither was confirmed, this end-to-end search illustrates how automated screening focuses computationally intensive substructure analyses on a few promising systems. Coupling multimodal agents to explicit forward modeling thus enables accurate, survey-scale lens analysis from macro mass profiles to small-scale dark matter structure.

2611.33658.abstract: We report the discovery of J0930+2902, the first carbon-enhanced metal-poor star with s-process enrichment (CEMP-s) identified in the GD-1 stellar stream, which is widely believed to originate from the tidal disruption of an old, metal-poor globular cluster. Using high-resolution Subaru/HDS spectroscopy, we present a comprehensive chemical abundance analysis of this star. Stellar atmospheric parameters were re-derived using Gaia photometry and parallaxes, combined with an iterative non-local thermodynamic equilibrium (NLTE) analysis of Fe lines. We determine abundances for 22 elements, including NLTE analyses of C, Na, Mg, Ca, Ti, Cr, Mn, Co, Sr, Y, Zr, Ba, and Eu. J0930+2902 exhibits pronounced enhancements of C, N, Na, and s-process elements, together with a low $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C ratio of 7.4, consistent with enrichment through binary mass transfer from a former asymptotic giant branch (AGB) companion. Large radial-velocity variations and a significant near-ultraviolet excess independently indicate the presence of a white dwarf companion, providing strong support for this scenario. Comparisons with FRUITY AGB nucleosynthesis models show that the residual neutron-capture abundance pattern is best reproduced by a low-mass AGB companion with an initial mass of approximately 3.0 $M_{\odot}$. Its enhancements of C, N, Na, and s-process elements make it chemically distinct from the other confirmed GD-1 members. These results identify J0930+2902 as a fossil record of binary mass transfer preserved in the ancient GD-1 stellar stream, demonstrating that binary interaction can leave long-lived chemical signatures in accreted stellar populations.

2611.34047.abstract: Efficient separation of unresolved point sources from extended objects (star-galaxy separation) is essential for deep wide-field imaging surveys, particularly at faint magnitudes where morphological differences become subtle. We assess two morphology-based classification methods applied to single-band, ground-based imaging from the Ultraviolet Near-Infrared Optical Northern Survey (UNIONS), using Euclid observations as a high-fidelity reference to evaluate their performance and to train one of the methods. We analysed 8 deg$^2$ of overlapping UNIONS $r$-band and Euclid $I_E$ data, comprising more than $7\times10^{5}$ sources. The Euclid data enable robust morphological labelling down to $I_E\simeq 26$, which we used to train and validate two classification approaches applied to UNIONS alone: a curve-of-growth method and a supervised neural-network classifier, both based on aperture photometry and image-quality information. The curve-of-growth method yields an almost perfectly complete point-source sample ($>95\%$), but its purity decreases rapidly at $r \simeq 22.5$. The neural-network approach significantly improves the purity at the faint end, maintaining $\geq 80\%$ purity down to $r \simeq 24$, while the completeness decreases to almost $50\%$ at similar depths. In both cases, performance strongly depends on the image quality of the ground-based data. This work shows how Euclid data can be used to develop, calibrate, and validate star-galaxy separation methods for ground-based surveys, useful in regions not covered by Euclid. Both methods have already been applied to UNIONS data and are readily applicable to future surveys such as LSST, offering flexible solutions depending on whether completeness or purity is prioritised.

2611.34111.abstract: We investigate correlations of halo and stellar spin axes in the TNG300 volume of the IllustrisTNG simulations and compare them with a model based on linear tidal torque theory (LTTT). Dark matter (DM) halo spin axes at $z = 0$ exhibit positive correlations as a function of Lagrangian pair separation. The LTTT-based model describes their separation dependence well, with weak variation in the fitted amplitude across mass thresholds. A Lagrangian-to-Eulerian separation mapping based on the conditional distributions of initial separations at fixed present-day separation, measured directly from the simulations, allows the model to reproduce the overall trends in both real and redshift space without additional fitting. The hydrodynamic and DM-only runs generally show similar DM halo spin-axis correlations, although the DM-only run exhibits a steeper rise at small real-space separations. In the hydrodynamic run, stellar spin-axis correlations are consistent with the same Lagrangian form as their DM halo counterparts, but with approximately 60% of the DM correlation amplitudes. Positive stellar correlations persist in both real and redshift space, and the mapped model captures their separation dependence. Initial spin-axis correlations of protohalos are substantially stronger than their present-day counterparts at the same Lagrangian separations, consistent with subsequent nonlinear spin evolution weakening these correlations. These results suggest that present-day halo and stellar spin-axis correlations retain signatures of the initial tidal field and that their general behavior can be understood through LTTT-based modeling combined with pair-separation mapping.

2611.34125.abstract: We report a recurring spectral artifact identified in observations obtained with the integral field unit (IFU) of the Gemini Multi-Object Spectrograph on the Gemini North telescope (GMOS-N). The artifact appears as a vertically aligned structure in reconstructed images of the IFU field of view, associated with a specific group of fibers and exhibiting a broad spectral feature around 8000~\AAng. Similar features were repeatedly identified in observations of different astronomical targets obtained between 2020 and 2022 using the R150 grating in the two-slit IFU mode. Taking advantage of the reproducibility of the artifact in the fiber and wavelength domains, we develop an empirical correction method in which the artifact is modeled as the product of a common spectral profile and a fiber-dependent amplitude distribution, with an overall normalization determined independently for each exposure. The artifact template is constructed from observations in which the affected fibers are largely separated from the astronomical source and subsequently applied to independent observations in which the artifact overlaps the source. The correction substantially suppresses the artificial spatial structure in the reconstructed images. Although the physical origin of the artifact remains unidentified, we present its observational characteristics and correction procedure to facilitate the identification and treatment of similar features by other GMOS-IFU users.

2611.34127.abstract:
Context. Supernova remnants (SNRs) are the final evolutionary stage of supernovae. In rare cases, the remnant persists as an optically luminous remnant decades after the explosion. We report the discovery of an unusual oxygen-rich (O-rich) SNR that was serendipitously discovered in the MUSE mosaic of the nearby (D $\sim$ 3.5 Mpc) galaxy NGC 253 released by arXiv:2506.14921.
Aims. We search for SNRs in MUSE integral field spectroscopy data of NGC 253.
Methods. We search for unresolved point sources with broad and strong [O III]$\lambda$$\lambda$4959,5007, [O I]$\lambda$$\lambda$6300,6364 or [O II]$\lambda$$\lambda$7320,7331 emission lines. We also search for possible counterparts at other wavelengths in archival data.
Results. We find a single O-rich SNR in NGC 253 with [O III]$\lambda$$\lambda$4959,5007. For this object, we report a coincident X-ray source detected by Chandra and a non-detection at mid-infrared wavelengths by JWST. Additionally, we identify [N II]$\lambda$$\lambda$6548,6583 emission lines and no detectable hydrogen or [SII]$\lambda$$\lambda$6716,6731 emission. The [N II] emission lines are broader (230 km/s) than the surrounding interstellar medium lines but still narrow in comparison to the [O III] emission (>1500 km/s) from the SNR. No detections of [O I]$\lambda$$\lambda$6300,6364 and [O II]$\lambda$$\lambda$7320,7331 were made.
Conclusions. The discovery of a single O-rich SNR after a systematic search of NGC 253 highlights their scarcity in nearby galaxies. The structure of [O III] emission indicates complex structure in the O-rich ejecta. The relative narrowness of [N II] emission lines compared to the [O III] lines and the non-detection of hydrogen show that the remnant is surrounded by an N-rich circumstellar medium. The ejecta is currently interacting with this material of the preceding supernova explosion.

2611.34325.abstract: Spider millisecond pulsars offer a direct route to constrain neutron-star masses, including candidates above two solar masses, via optical light-curve modeling of the irradiated companion. This assumes stable irradiation. We report new $g'r'i'$ photometry of the redback PSR~J2215+5135 from the Iranian National Observatory in 2024 and compare it with the 2014 data of \citet{linares2018peering}. Peak brightness and orbital period are unchanged within uncertainties, but the light-curve wings are significantly broader in 2024, as the local deviations exceed $3\sigma$ on the rising branch in all filters, with an additional $i'$-band excess on the falling branch, giving a global permutation-test significance of $4.26\sigma$. A single-hot-spot model fits the 2024 data better than a spot-free one, but systematic residuals remain. The broader wings are reproduced only through correlated shifts in the spot, inclination, filling factor and companion temperature, which we regard as model compensation, not physics. An extended, variable heating component may also fit. The best-fit spot temperature differs between epochs by about $1060$\,K, comparable to its model dependence (about $900$\,K between two codes for 2014), so we do not interpret this as physical. Two epochs cannot show whether the change is gradual, sudden or short-lived. The inferred neutron-star mass depends on the spot treatment: $2.13^{+0.16}_{-0.13}\,M_\odot$ for 2014 with a hot spot, and $M_\mathrm{NS}=1.95^{+0.11}_{-0.07}\,M_\odot$ for 2024. These agree within about $1\sigma$, but come from differently shaped light curves, and the statistical uncertainties exclude heating-prescription systematics.

2611.34404.abstract: G22.7$-$0.2 is a middle-aged supernova remnant (SNR; $\tau \sim 3\times10^4$ yr) interacting with the nearby giant molecular cloud GMC 23.3$-$0.4. A handful of X-ray sources have been identified within the SNR radio shell by previous XMM-Newton and NuSTAR observations. In particular, three of those X-ray sources (N1, N2, and N3) have been detected above 10 keV, indicating that they are either X-ray point sources, or molecular cloud clumps heated by SNR blast waves. In the latter case, non-thermal bremsstrahlung or synchrotron radiation from shock-heated molecular clouds may appear as extended X-ray sources. We conducted an X-ray survey of the SNR-cloud interaction region with Chandra and detected 23 X-ray sources with $> 5\sigma$ significance using wavdetect, 20 of which were previously uncataloged. The sub-arcsecond angular resolution of Chandra allowed us to spatially resolve these X-ray sources. After accounting for point spread function (PSF) smearing and dust scattering effects, we determine that two NuSTAR hard X-ray sources (N1 and N2) are extended, whereas the other Chandra sources are point sources. While N1 may be a compact filament or a synchrotron-emitting clump with $r\sim0.018$ pc, our analysis suggests that N2 is likely a compact cloud clump shock-heated by the SNR and emitting non-thermal bremsstrahlung or synchrotron X-rays, with $r\sim0.052$ pc and $M\approx0.6$ $M_\odot$ under the non-thermal bremsstrahlung model.

2611.34496.abstract: Very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) observations show that a fraction of active galactic nucleus (AGN) jets exhibit pronounced apparent bending on parsec scales, potentially strongly enhanced by projection effects. While individual sources have been studied in detail, the statistical properties of curved jets and the physical mechanisms responsible for their morphology remain poorly constrained. We aim to select a statistically robust sample of AGNs with significantly curved parsec-scale jets and to constrain the physical mechanisms responsible for jet bending. We analyse 123 456 VLBI images of 17 478 AGNs collected by the public Astrogeo database. After filtering for extended structure, we extract and stack multi-epoch, multi-frequency (1.2--86 GHz) ridge lines. We fit linear and logarithmic helices representing jet precession and resonant Kelvin--Helmholtz instability mode. We combine model-fits and Monte Carlo simulations to further constrain these physical models. We robustly identify 586 AGNs (7.4% of sources with resolved jets) with curved parsec-scale jets. Compared to straight jets, curved ones are less common at low redshifts, possibly due to the sample-related selection effects. In the precession scenario, the inferred periods span $P \sim$10--10 000 yr, with a logarithmic mean of $\sim 220$ yr. Solid-body disc precession in supermassive black hole binaries is broadly consistent with these periods, whereas geodetic precession requires extremely tight, near-equal-mass systems. Lense--Thirring precession remains viable for both thin and thick discs. Kelvin--Helmholtz instability also provides a potential explanation. However, identifying the preferred model for each individual source requires further investigation, including temporal analysis and jet kinematics.

2611.34577.abstract: Amorphous solid water (ASW) dominates interstellar ice mantles, but its porosity, density, optical response, and mechanical stability depend sensitively on how the ice is grown. Here, we present the characterization capabilities of COSPINU2, a cryogenic ultra-high-vacuum set-up designed to prepare and diagnose water ice films under controlled background and doser-assisted deposition conditions. The instrument combines a calibrated gas-handling line, near- and mid-infrared Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, HeNe interferometry, broad-beam optical imaging, and quadrupole mass spectrometry. We demonstrate how these complementary diagnostics provide a coherent description of ASW films grown between 10K and 150K. For background-grown ices, a dual-angle interferometric method is used to retrieve refractive indices near 632 nm, while near-infrared interference fringes provide thickness calibration. The results show that lower deposition temperatures and higher growth rates produce films with lower refractive indices and stronger dangling-OH infrared signatures, consistent with the formation of more porous ASW. We also show that pressure-based density estimates are unreliable in the background geometry because cryopumping decouple chamber pressure from the local substrate flux. For doser-grown films, optical interference imaging allows reconstruction of dome-shaped thickness profiles and estimation of effective densities. Finally, sudden restructuring events are observed in thick (above 2 micrometers), low-temperature porous ASW films, evidenced by abrupt changes in interferometric contrast, optical scattering, and dangling-OH features. These results establish COSPINU2 as a versatile platform for quantitative water-ice characterization and provide the physical baseline required for future studies of infrared irradiation and optical constants of interstellar ice analogues.
